newsitem.title: USA: Low jobless rate means labor shortages-Chicago Fed.
newsitem.headline: Low jobless rate means labor shortages-Chicago Fed.

text.p: Michael Moskow, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, said there is no question low unemployment levels result in labor shortages.

"There's no question as you get to those low levels of unemployment we are at today that you see specific categories of the workforce where there are shortages," Moskow told reporters during a conference here.
"We certainly hear about shortages in certain key areas," he said of the Midwest.
The Chicago Fed held a conference around the presentation of results of a year-long study of the Midwest economy.

"There is a shortage in the Midwest, and a nationwide shortage, in the software area. In the marketplace, the relative wages of these people, those categories, should go up to attract more people into those specific areas," he added.
But Moskow also said the Midwest was not reporting increases in employment benefits above the national average.
Moskow, in a paper released at the conference, pointed out that while labor markets have "tightened considerably, the Midwest has yet to see a complete recovery in terms of per capita income."
The Chicago Fed president also noted that the labor market reflects a "very dynamic process as you see people moving in and out" of the workforce.
Manufacturing and agriculture have revived their competitive fortunes, but they continue to require fewer employees because of improved technology and new production methods, Moskow said.
He noted that employment was growing more slowly in the Midwest than in the rest of the country because so many individuals are already employed.
